question.knowledge_point: Computing the One-Sided Limits of a Piecewise Function when the Limits Coincide
question.problem:
Find the limit at $x=\frac{1}{2}$ of the piecewise function $f(x)$ defined by

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}6x+1\, & \text{ for }\,x\le \frac{1}{2} \\ -4{log}_{2}⁡x\, & \text{ for }\,x>\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
Approaching from the left, we have $x<\frac{1}{2},$ so we use the expression $f(x)=6x+1.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {(1/2)}^{-}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {(1/2)}^{-}}(6x+1) \\  & =6\cdot \frac{1}{2}+1 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Now,  approaching from the right, we have $x>\frac{1}{2},$ so we use the expression $f(x)=-4{log}_{2}⁡x.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {(1/2)}^{+}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {(1/2)}^{+}}-4{log}_{2}⁡x \\  & =-4{log}_{2}⁡\frac{1}{2} \\  & =-4{log}_{2}⁡{2}^{-1} \\  & =-4(-1){log}_{2}⁡2 \\  & =-4(-1) \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the left- and right-sided limits are equal to $4,$ we conclude that

$$
{lim}_{x\to (1/2)}f(x)=4.
$$

judgment.reasoning: All three earlier answers are confirmed by independent mathematics and their respective captured worked solutions. For q-36720, the left limit is 6(1/2)+1=4 and the right limit is -4 log_2(1/2)=4, so the two-sided limit is 4. For q-36724, the left limit is the cube root of 8, which is 2, while the right limit is cos(3π)=-1; unequal one-sided limits mean the two-sided limit does not exist. For q-37488, approaching zero from the left uses tan(x), which tends to 0. The choice's LaTeX spacing command does not change its equivalence to the source answer.
